b)       Community Wildfire Protection Plan Presentation
                   Staff Report (Fire Protection)

                                                                                                         July 20^ 2020
                                                                                                            Page 6 of 9




Conor Corbett from Diamond Head Consulting was the lead contact for the project and presented the
findings of the plan to Council at the July 20^^ Meeting. Some of the highlights of the CWPP are as follows:

             o   The previous work in 2002 to establish an interface Fire Hazard Planning Model in our
                 developments has been effective in lowering the interface risk in Langford (pg. 13)
             o   The overall rating for the City is listed as High, however there is additional work can be done
                 to lower the risk further (pg 51)
             o   There are 27 recommendations, many of which can receive additional funding from UBCM
                 to implement that are now possible with the CWPP completed (pgs. i-iv)
             o   Recommendations include measures to manage forest fuel, provide community education,
                 enhance wildfire response and integrate FireSmart planning further into developments.

In order to qualify for UBCM funding, the CWPP needs to adhere to strict guidelines. As a result, the CWPP
does not specifically address private land which accounts for 49% of Langford. However, the
recommendations of the CWPP for the other classes of properties can be used by City Staff to work with
individual home owners or neighbourhoods to help mitigate the interface threat for private property.

In addition, the report recommends the City forming partnerships with surrounding land owners, specifically
CRD Water and BC Parks to help further reduce the risk from wildfire and both agencies are receptive to
working together on these initiatives.

     a)   BYLAW NO. 1864
          "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 574, (Omnibus No. 52 - Residential Zone Combining),
          Bylaw No. 1864, 2020"

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1846 at 5:49 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Bylaw No. 1864 proposes to amend Zoning Bylaw
No. 300 by reducing all one- and two-family and small lot residential zones into just three types of zones:
small lot, one- and two-family residential, and lakeshore residential.

                                                                                                        July 20^ 2020
                                                                                                           Page 2 of 9




Bylaw No. 1864 proposes the following broad changes to Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
• The consolidation of the Residential Small Lot 1 (RSI), Residential Small Lot 2 (RS2), and Residential
    Small Lot 3 (RS3) zones into a single Residential Small Lot 1 zone, where the principal permitted use is a
    one-family dwelling without a suite on lots as small as 200m2, and a one-family dwelling with a suite on
    lots that are not less than 400m2;
•   The consolidation of the One-Family Residential (Rl), the One-and Two-Family Residential (R2), the One-
    and Two-Family Residential A (R2A), the One-to Five Family Residential (R3), the One- Family Residential
    4 (R4) and Residential Small Lot 4 (RS4) zone into a single One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) zone
    where the minimum lot size for a single-family dwelling with a suite is 400m2 and the minimum lot size
    for a two-family dwelling is 600m2 (subject to certain conditions such as lot width);
•   The creation of a new Residential Lakeshore 1 (RLl) zone which encompasses all residential lots that
    are directly adjacent to Florence, Langford and Glen Lake and holds them to their current zoning with
    respect to land use and density under either One-Family Residential (Rl) zone or the One- and Two-
    Family Residential (R2) and the One-and Two-Family Residential A (R2A) zones;
•   Various amendments to Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in order to affect the changes listed
    above;
•   Amending the minimum lot size for a two-family dwelling in the CD12 (South Skirt Mountain) zone to
    bring parity between that zone and the CD3 (Westhills) zone in regards to lot size for a two-family
    residential use;

Advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

None presented.

None presented.

for Bylaw No. 1864 closed at 5:51 p.m.

            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 502, (2955 Irwin Rd), 2017".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1731 at 5:31 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                            Page 2 of 9



The City Planner advised that Duncan Magee with Keycorp Developments has applied to amend the zoning
of 2955 Irwin Road from the RR4 (Rural Residential 4) Zone to the RS3 (Residential Small Lot) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of an 18 lot small lot subdivision that will
include trail and park improvements.

This proposal is consistent with the Hillside and Shoreline policy designation within Langford's Official
Community Plan.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

As a bonus for increased density the applicant has agreed to provide the following in accordance with
Council policy:

$ 6,000 per lot or $3960 per small lot towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

$1000 per lot or $660 per small lot towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

A resident on Ravensview Drive thanked Council for a job well done on recent infrastructure projects.
Noted that the developer is going to great lengths to make this a good project. Raised concerns about
water on Ravensview Drive, in particular low water problems. The resident asked that this be checked on.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1731 closed at 5:36 p.m.

Councillor Seaton arrived at 5:44pnn.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 468, (2874 Leigh Rd), 2017".

interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                             Page 3 of 9



The City Planner advised that Carole Hutchinson of Design One — Stevens Interiors has applied on behalf
of Derek Hass to amend the text of the R1 (One- and Two-Family) Zone to allow a secondary suite in an
accessory building at 2874 Leigh Road.


As part of this application, a Public Hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide a Section 219 Covenant registered
in priority of all other charges on title that agrees that:

1.    All frontage improvements, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, be constructed or that
      cash-in-lieu of sidewalks, in an amount to be determined by the Director of Engineering be paid to
      the City, prior to Building Permit issuance.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside and Shoreline designation.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy. Staff have received
three letters of support for the application and one letter of concern. These letters have been included
in the Public Hearing package.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.


Resident on Kiwi Road gave okay for project with certain conditions. Concerned that there may be a bigger
garage for the surrounding site. Also concerned of decks, windows and doors facing his yard. Lastly,
concerned about the potential sale and safety of his yard.


Matthew Baldwin provided clarification. Existing house will be a garage with secondary new suite in
location of existing garage.


Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

The owner of the property provided clarification. Secondary suite will be close to the water. New principle
dwelling will be where the garage is now, but will be slightly closer to the neighbouring property. The
owner also clarified window positions and screening in neighbouring yard.

Mayor Young asked for a letter saying that it will be owner occupied.


The owner is committed to share plans with neighbours.

the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1736 closed at 5:49 p.m.

Acting Mayor Seaton advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or

contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. A/Mayor Seaton advised that after
everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                      Page 2 of 8




The City Planner advised that the City of Langford is proposing to make various omnibus amendments to
the City of Langford's Zoning Bylaw No. 300. These amendments include:
     •   generally increasing the maximum height permitted for apartment buildings from four storeys to
         six storeys;
     •   changing the ground floor parking requirements in the C8 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian)
         zone;
     •   adding "apartment" as a permitted use on two properties in the Business and Technology 1 (BT1)
         zone,

         the zoning boundary; and
     •   allowing shipping containers as a permitted accessory use to mini-storage

Government Act. This proposal is consistent with Official Community Plan Designations. Advertisements
have been placed as required by Council policy.

if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that the City of Langford has applied to amend the text of the Zoning Bylaw 300
in regards to permit the inclusion of Community Care Facilities to the list of uses allowed in the M1 (Light
Industrial) Zone.

Bylaw 1684 will amend the text within the Zoning Bylaw so that 'Care Facilities' will be permitted in the
M1 (Light Industrial) Zone.

As a light industrial zone, industrial businesses that operate within the M1 zone do not produce noxious
odours, dust, smoke or noise that would negatively impact the surrounding non-industrial uses. The
majority of parcels currently zoned M1 in Langford are found along Dunford Avenue, and act as a
transitionary industrial space separating heavier industrial uses and residential zones.

As many care facilities require expansive areas in order to congregate and assist to their clients, industrial
space within the Ml, light industrial, zone would be appropriate for adult patrons to receive care.

The bylaw being proposed would restrict care to adults and would not permit patrons or those providing
care to reside on parcels within the M1 zone as part of the care facility.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

This proposal is consistent with the Neighbourhood Official Community Plan designations.

Advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The City Planner advised that the City of Langford has applied to amend the text of the Zoning Bylaw 300
in regards to permit the inclusion of Community Care Facilities to the list of uses allowed in the M1 (Light
Industrial) Zone.

Bylaw 1684 will amend the text within the Zoning Bylaw so that 'Care Facilities' will be permitted in the
M1 (Light Industrial) Zone.

As a light industrial zone, industrial businesses that operate within the M1 zone do not produce noxious
odours, dust, smoke or noise that would negatively impact the surrounding non-industrial uses. The
majority of parcels currently zoned M1 in Langford are found along Dunford Avenue, and act as a
transitionary industrial space separating heavier industrial uses and residential zones.

As many care facilities require expansive areas in order to congregate and assist to their clients, industrial
space within the Ml, light industrial, zone would be appropriate for adult patrons to receive care.

The bylaw being proposed would restrict care to adults and would not permit patrons or those providing
care to reside on parcels within the M1 zone as part of the care facility.

            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 514, (2844 Millstream Rd), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1748 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or
her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after

heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Pascal Toupin- Selinger with Ironclad Developments has applied on behalf
of Andre Louis Cottyn to amend the zoning of 2844 Millstream Rd from the CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone
to the MUlA (Mixed Use Residential Commercial A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to include the subject parcel in plans to construct an apartment building
on 720, 724 and 732 Meaford Avenue.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


1.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
     unit, which may be reduced by 75% if rental tenure is secured for a term of no less than 10 years, prior
     to subdivision approval:


     a)     $2,562 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
     b)     $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
other charges on title, that agrees to the following:


           i.That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of the
              Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
           ii.That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
              Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision approval or building
              permit issuance, whichever is first;
          iii.That the applicant acknowledges and agrees to design the proposed development, in accordance
              to the updated parking regulations as determined by Council, to the discretion of the Director of
              Planning;
          iv.That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and to
              complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site infrastructure
          necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the applicant's expense;
       v.That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements, including, but not limited to, the
          installation of a sidewalk to the corner of Meaford and Millstream Road to align with the sidewalk
          infrastructure required along Meaford Road, in accordance with Bylaw No.1000 and to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or building permit
          issuance, whichever is first;
      vi.That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or
          other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense; and
      vii.That the applicant acknowledges the proximity to industrial business operators may be a nuisance

records.original_motion_text: That Council: 1. Direct staff to prepare a bylaw in accordance with the proposal to amend the zoning designation of the properties located at 647 and 667 Redington Avenue and 2478 and 2482 Selwyn Road from the R2 (One and Two-Family Dwelling) zone to the RM7A (Medium Density Apartment) and BP1A (Millstream Road East) Zone, and to prepare a bylaw to amend the OCP for a portion of the subject property from the Neighbourhood to the Mixed Use Employment Center designation, subject to the following terms and conditions: a) That the owner agrees to provide as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per dwelling unit prior to subdivision approval: i) $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund (Less the cost of the trail connection, should Council find this appropriate); and ii) $661 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund. b) That prior to first reading, the applicant prepare a cost estimate to build the trail so Council can consider if they wish to lessen the required amenity contributions by the cost of the trail as this will provide a localized amenity for the neighbourhood. c) That the applicant provide, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority over all other charges on title, that agrees to the following; i) Provide the following recommendations from the Boulevard Traffic Impact Report as part of the works and services installed prior to issuance of a Building Permit: i. Provide a "Keep Circulatory Lane Clear" (or similar) sign for northbound Redington Avenue traffic at the McCallum roundabout entry point; and ii. On-site pedestrian walkway connection be provided between the Redington side and Selwyn side of the site. That the developer build the 1.8m wide gravel trail to Bylaw 1000 standards (Schedule 13 Trail Standards with trailhead bollard) from Selwyn Road to Bellamy Link prior to issuance of the first Building Permit on the land; and iii) That the developer provide a construction management parking plan as a condition of rezoning and to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a Development Permit. iv) That the applicant provide the required FUS calculations prior to subdivision or building permit, whichever comes first. 2. Amend BP1A zone to: a. Include mini storage as a permitted use for the relevant portion of 667 Redington Avenue and to exclude the property from all other permitted uses; b. Separate the gross floor area from the overall maximum of the BP1A zone and restrict the mini storage site to 8,500m2 of gross floor area; c. Require a 3m interior side yard setback for the interior lot line that abuts the dwellings along Redington Avenue and Skedans Road; and d. To allow the subject property of 667 Redington to have 75% lot coverage for the mini-storage business. 3. Amend the RM7A zone to: a. Have the minimum lot size reduced from 4,000m2 to 3,000m2. b. To allow the subject property to have an FSR of 1.2; and c. To permit the subject property to have 5 storeys in height for the two apartment buildings. 4. Direct the applicant to redesign the townhouse site plan to conform to the interior side yard lot line as part of the Development Permit process.

3.     PUBLIC HEARINGS


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1717
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 507, (2500 Echo Valley Dr), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1717 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that
his or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the
matters contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw
should give their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that
after everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to
be heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                           March 19th, 2018
                                                                                               Page 2 of 14



The City Planner advised that Rachael Sansom of Turner Lane Development Corp. has applied on
behalf of 1085540 BC Ltd. to amend the text of "Area 2" in the CD6 (Comprehensive Development
6 — Bear Mountain) Zone to allow for a townhouse development at 2500 Echo Valley Drive.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the
Local Government Act. In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the
following items prior to Public Hearing:


1. A detailed site plan illustrating two routes for access to and egress from the site;
2. A stormwater management plan; and
3.   Confirmation of adequate water, fire flow and sanitary sewer capacities to serve the
      proposed development; and


The applicant has submitted the required access plan, and a Servicing Feasibility Study to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering (it should be noted that the study has been approved
for conceptual stormwater management only, all other servicing is subject to detailed design
approval. Detailed stormwater calculations will be required during site servicing and will be
subject to further approvals by the City).


The applicant has also agreed to provide a Section 219 Covenant, prior to Bylaw Adoption,
addressing frontage improvements, stormwater management, water supply, road access to
adjacent properties, local service agreements and firefighting provisions.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.


Concurrent with this application, Council may also wish to consider discharging a Covenant
registered as a condition of rezoning for the properties located at 1410 Grand Forest Close, 1431
Grand Forest Close and 2342 Lairds Gate which are adjacent to the subject property.                  This
Covenant was registered at the request of the previous owner of 2500 Echo Valley Drive in order
to restrict development of these adjacent properties to minimize the potential impact of
development on the property at 2500 Echo Valley Drive.


Ownership of 2500 Echo Valley has since changed, and the new owner wishes to develop the
property as evidenced by this application. Council may therefore wish to discharge the Covenant
on 1410 Grand Forest Close, 1431 Grand Forest Close and 2342 Lairds Gate in advance of the 5
year timeline expiry date.

The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

None presented.

Acting Mayor called a second time for presentations.

                                                                                                     Page 3 of 14


None presented.


The Acting Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Acting Mayor
officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1717 closed at 5:35 p.m.

THAT Council:

        1. Consider bringing forward Bylaw No. 2248 for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd readings at a
        future Council meeting in order to amend the text of the Residential Townhouse
        1 (RT1) Zone to allow secondary suites in townhomes at 1234 Goldstream
        Avenue subject to the following terms and conditions:

        a. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219 covenant
        in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        i.That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit
        for the proposed development agreeing that the garages are to be used for the
        parking of vehicles and not the storage of items preventing the parking of
        vehicles therein.

        ii. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
        exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
        Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
        Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product
        Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
        Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
        requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

        iii. That a strata plan may not be registered for more than seven (7) units;

        iv.That the buildings be constructed with electric heat pumps for each unit, or
        an equivalent electric centralized system that allow each unit to control their
        own temperature, be installed prior to issuance of an occupancy permit;








        v.That the buildings be constructed such that residential parking spaces
        (excluding visitor parking spaces) meets the requirements set out in Section
        4.01.08(2) and (3) of the Zoning Bylaw;

        vi. That a maximum of two (2) secondary suites be permitted on the property.

        vii. That three (3) visitor parking stalls be provided.

        AND

        2. Direct staff to amend the definition of suite and secondary suite within Bylaw
        No. 2248, as outlined within the January 19, 2026, staff report.

candidates.motion_text:
THAT Council:

        1. Consider bringing forward Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 707 (2614,
        2616, 2618, 2622, 2626 Peatt Road and 2622, 2625 and 2629 Sunderland Road)
        Bylaw No. 2146, 2025 for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd readings at a future Council meeting
        in order to amend the zoning designation of the properties located at 2614-2622
        Peatt Road and 2622-2629 Sunderland Road from the One and Two Family
        Residential (R2) Zone to Area 2 of the City Centre Pedestrian (CCP) Zone subject
        to the following terms and conditions:

        a. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
        contributions per dwelling unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:

        i.$610 per residential unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

        ii. $2,318 per residential unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and

        iii. $10.75 per m2 of commercial gross floor area toward the General Amenity
        Reserve Fund

        subject to reductions in accordance with the Affordable Housing and Amenity
        Contribution Policy and the Attainable Housing Policy depending on use and
        height.

        b. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219 covenant
        in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        i. That the following be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards
        to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a
        building permit:

        1. Full frontage improvements on Peatt Road and Sunderland Road;







2.Full frontage improvements on the southern active transportation corridor,
including a paved multi-use path, street trees on both sides of the path, street
lighting, and bike racks.

3.Road extensions and intersection improvements in accordance with the
recommendations from the approved Traffic Impact Assessment,

4. A right-in and right-out at Peatt and Arncote if this does not exist at the time
of Building Permit; and

5. A storm water management plan.

ii. That the following be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards
to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to any land alteration:

1.A construction parking and delivery management plan; and

2. A mitigation plan.

iii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit
for the proposed development that ensures residential parking is allocated to
each unit as required by the zoning bylaw and are not provided in exchange for
compensation separate from that of a residential unit;

iv. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type Ill Environmental Product
Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

v. That, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the developer enters into a
Housing Agreement with the City that requires either a minimum 10% of units
constructed be rented for at least 10% below the benchmark rent for the unit
type for a term not less than 25 years or that a minimum of 5% of the units
constructed be directed to and sold in accordance with the terms of the
Attainable Home Ownership Program Policy (POL-0166-PLAN). The developer
shall identify the Attainable Units on the plans submitted for the required
Development Permit application;

vi. That individual electric heat pumps for each unit, or an equivalent electric
central system, be installed prior to issuance of an occupancy permit;

vii. That the parcels associated with this development be consolidated prior to
issuance of a Development Permit and that the drawings submitted for approval
as part of the Development Permit application substantially comply with what
has been presented to Council through this rezoning application (Z23-0002).

viii. That a demolition permit for any of the homes on the subject properties not
be issued until a building permit associated with the proposed development has
been applied for;








ix.That 10% of the residential units be designed and built as 3-bedroom units;

x. That the Maintenance Plan in regards to the existing dwellings and properties
that was presented by the applicant at the time of rezoning be included as an
appendix to the required covenant prior to adoption and adhered to at all times;

xi. That no portion of a building adjoining the western interior side lot line shall
be constructed unless it's a maximum 4 storeys in height, includes a rooftop
amenity space, and provides an architecturally treated facade that addresses
heat reflection, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Community Planning and
Development;

xii. That the following shall be provided to the satisfaction of the Director of
Community Planning and Development:

1.An on-site landscape plan that includes public gathering spaces including
benches and seating areas along the southern active transportation corridor.
The approved landscape plan will form part of the Development Permit for the
site.

2.Prior to the issuance of a Development Permit, a statutory right of way
registered on title in priority of all other charges, to secure public access to the
public spaces shown on the approved landscape plan.

AND

2. Authorize the Director of Community Planning and Development to grant the
following variance within the Development Permit for Form and Character:

a. That Sections 6.58.06(1)(b) and 6.58.06(2)(b) be varied to reduce the interior
side yard setbacks for the portion of a building 2-storeys or less and the portion
of a building 3-storeys or higher from 3.0m (9.8 ft) to 1.5m (5.0 ft).

5. A storm water management plan.

ii. That the following be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards
to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to any land alteration:

1.A construction parking and delivery management plan; and

2. A mitigation plan.

iii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit
for the proposed development that ensures residential parking is allocated to
each unit as required by the zoning bylaw and are not provided in exchange for
compensation separate from that of a residential unit;

iv. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or
exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on
Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type Ill Environmental Product
Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming
Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the
requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

v. That, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the developer enters into a
Housing Agreement with the City that requires either a minimum 10% of units
constructed be rented for at least 10% below the benchmark rent for the unit
type for a term not less than 25 years or that a minimum of 5% of the units
constructed be directed to and sold in accordance with the terms of the
Attainable Home Ownership Program Policy (POL-0166-PLAN). The developer
shall identify the Attainable Units on the plans submitted for the required
Development Permit application;

vi. That individual electric heat pumps for each unit, or an equivalent electric
central system, be installed prior to issuance of an occupancy permit;

vii. That the parcels associated with this development be consolidated prior to
issuance of a Development Permit and that the drawings submitted for approval
as part of the Development Permit application substantially comply with what
has been presented to Council through this rezoning application (Z23-0002).

viii. That a demolition permit for any of the homes on the subject properties not
be issued until a building permit associated with the proposed development has
been applied for;








ix.That 10% of the residential units be designed and built as 3-bedroom units;

x. That the Maintenance Plan in regards to the existing dwellings and properties
that was presented by the applicant at the time of rezoning be included as an
appendix to the required covenant prior to adoption and adhered to at all times;

xi. That no portion of a building adjoining the western interior side lot line shall
be constructed unless it's a maximum 4 storeys in height, includes a rooftop
amenity space, and provides an architecturally treated facade that addresses
heat reflection, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Community Planning and
Development;

xii. That the following shall be provided to the satisfaction of the Director of
Community Planning and Development:

1.An on-site landscape plan that includes public gathering spaces including
benches and seating areas along the southern active transportation corridor.
The approved landscape plan will form part of the Development Permit for the
site.

2.Prior to the issuance of a Development Permit, a statutory right of way
registered on title in priority of all other charges, to secure public access to the
public spaces shown on the approved landscape plan.

AND

2. Authorize the Director of Community Planning and Development to grant the
following variance within the Development Permit for Form and Character:

a. That Sections 6.58.06(1)(b) and 6.58.06(2)(b) be varied to reduce the interior
side yard setbacks for the portion of a building 2-storeys or less and the portion
of a building 3-storeys or higher from 3.0m (9.8 ft) to 1.5m (5.0 ft).

        a)   BYLAW NO. 1746
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 512, {Omnibus No. 49 - Various Amendments),
             2017".


The Mayoropened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1746 at 5:40 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
 has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that The City is proposing various amendments to Zoning Bylaw No. 300 to fulfill
 Council resolutions and address issues that have been brought to staffs attention.

These amendments include: allowing crematoria in the BP2A, BP4, BPS and M2 Zones (to clarify what is
 already permitted as a "general industrial use"); reducing the minimum setbacks for children's play
 equipment for group daycares; allowing offices in the CSl Zone; removing references to deleted sections
 in the MUIA Zone; allowing the Director of Planning to vary minimum setbacks to minimize potential
 impacts on environmentally sensitive areas; allowing a variety oftownhouse configurations (number of
 units per townhouse block); regulating maximum driveway widths for small lot and townhouse
 development; and amending the requirements for secondarysuite parking.

 As part of this application, a Public Hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
 Government Act. Council may wish to proceed with the Public Hearing at this time, as there are no
 requirements for additional information prior to the Hearing.

 Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

 The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

 None presented.

PUBLIC HEARINGS


       3.1     BYLAW NO. 1998

               The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1998 at 5:34 pm.

        Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Roya Adami has applied to
        amend the zoning of 2619 Sooke Road from One- and Two-Family Residential {R2) Zone
        to the Neighbourhood Institutional (PIA) Zone, and to amend the text of the PIA zone
        to allow for a 44-child Group Daycare.

        As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
        regulations of the Local Government Act.

        In support ofthis application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following prior to
        Bylaw Adoption:

        a. $6,000.00 for a sidewalk on the Sooke Rd. frontage ofthestrata property, to the
        satisfaction of the Directorof Engineering.

        This proposal is consistent with the current Official Community Plan "Neighbourhood
        Centre" designation

        Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
        Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations. None.


Mayor Young called a second time for presentations. None.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the
Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1998 closed at 5:35 p.m.

3.2     BYLAW NO. 1856

       The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1856 at 5:35 pm.
        Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Rachael Sansom has applied
       on behalfof 1177016 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 2627 and 2631 Millstream Road
       from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential Zone to the RM9 (Medium Density
       Apartment) Zone.

       This is being proposed in order to allow for the development ofan apartment building
       with approximately 113 units.

       As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
       regulations of the Local Government Act.

       In support ofthis application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
       a) As a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per residential unit,
       prior to issuance of a building permit:

i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund;
ii. $3,660 towards the General Annenity Reserve Fund;
iii. (i) and (ii) are subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance
with the Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy;
iv. That the total amount of contribution, after reductions, to the General Amenity
Reserve Fund may be reduced by the estimated cost of installing additional sidewalk in
front of the properties located at 2635 Millstream Road and 2623-2579 Millstream
Road, as well as the cost of installing a flashing pedestrian crossing, to the satisfaction of
the Director of Engineering;

b) That, prior to BylawAdoption, the developer:

1.    Provides a Section 219 covenant registered in priority of all other charges on title
that agrees to the following:

1. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards
to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior the issuance of a building permit:

a. Full frontage improvements, including the installation of sidewalks along the
frontage of the properties and along the frontage of 2635 Millstream Road and 2623-
2579 Millstream Road, as well as the installation of a flashing pedestrian crossing.
b.     A storm water management plan;
c.    A construction parking management plan

2. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades required to the
services and utilities required for the development;


3. That the developer registers a strata plan, prior to the issuance of an occupancy
permit, that creates individual strata titles for each resident unit;


4. That the developer consolidates the properties prior to the issuance of a
development permit;



5. That the required parking stalls for this development are allocated for the use by
 individuals in each unit and visitors, as required by Bylaw No. 300, and that parking is
not separated from individual units nor provided in exchange for compensation
separate than that of the residential unit; and
 a.    That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
parking space; and
 b.    Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging; and

        c. Where an electric vehicle energy nnanagement system is implemented (load
        sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
        ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
        d. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
        operation and the Strata Council may not preventan owner, occupant, or tenant from
        installing the EV charging equipment.

        This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood
        designation.

        Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
        Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.


        Rachael Sansom, 1498 White Pine Terrace - The applicant has addressed concerns
        though larger setbacks, sidewalks, and flashing pedestrian crossing. The density allows
        for more families in a smaller area.



        Marguerite Coady, 682 Charmar Cres - Appreciate the new sidewalks. Request
        neighbourhood parking designation rather than City Centre parking.


       Jessie Priest, 2849 Lake End Rd - Support this project. We need more housing, support
        building up not out.


       Amber Baker, 2670Winster Rd - Supportdevelopment. Pleased there will be sufficient
       parking, support the proposed light-controlled crossing.


       Dana Elizabeth, 2850Aldwynd Rd - Supportthis application, we need more affordable
       housing options. Support EV charging and crosswalks.


       Kevin Jones, 472 Regency PI - Support this, we need more affordable housing.

       Lane Britton, 3022 Shoreview Dr - Support this, this is an opportunity for affordable
       housing.


       Laurie Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terr-Meeting ID number was incorrect on Friday, will
       Council consider postponing the hearing.

            Marie Watmough, Acting Director of Corporate Services - The correct number was
            posted on Saturday and the notices were correct.


            Tony Zarskias, 3645 Tillicum Rd - Calling in to represent a Langford business. It's
            important to build up, not out.


            Albert Internicola, 670 Marlisa PI - It's people who don't live in the neighbourhood who
            support this. Neighbourhood can't support 113 more vehicles. Do not support.


            Ron Bain, 719 Massie Dr - Do not support, roads are already at maximum capacity.


     Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.


            Tom Miller, 661 Marlisa PI - Do not support, the proposed development is too tall.
            Other people calling in don't understand that the neighbourhood is already dense.


            Albert Internicola, 670 Marlisa PI - Building will shadow neighbourhood, would support
            a smaller building.



            Jacqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Dr - A number of issues with this development
            that were brought up earlier have not been addressed. If approved, the parking
            designation should be Neighbourhood and not City Centre.


     Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the
     Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1856 closed at 6:02 p.m.

4.   ADOPTION OF COUNCIL MINUTES

        c. Where an electric vehicle energy nnanagement system is implemented (load
        sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
        ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
        d. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
        operation and the Strata Council may not preventan owner, occupant, or tenant from
        installing the EV charging equipment.

        This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood
        designation.

        Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
        Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.


        Rachael Sansom, 1498 White Pine Terrace - The applicant has addressed concerns
        though larger setbacks, sidewalks, and flashing pedestrian crossing. The density allows
        for more families in a smaller area.



        Marguerite Coady, 682 Charmar Cres - Appreciate the new sidewalks. Request
        neighbourhood parking designation rather than City Centre parking.


       Jessie Priest, 2849 Lake End Rd - Support this project. We need more housing, support
        building up not out.


       Amber Baker, 2670Winster Rd - Supportdevelopment. Pleased there will be sufficient
       parking, support the proposed light-controlled crossing.


       Dana Elizabeth, 2850Aldwynd Rd - Supportthis application, we need more affordable
       housing options. Support EV charging and crosswalks.


       Kevin Jones, 472 Regency PI - Support this, we need more affordable housing.

       Lane Britton, 3022 Shoreview Dr - Support this, this is an opportunity for affordable
       housing.


       Laurie Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terr-Meeting ID number was incorrect on Friday, will
       Council consider postponing the hearing.

            Marie Watmough, Acting Director of Corporate Services - The correct number was
            posted on Saturday and the notices were correct.


            Tony Zarskias, 3645 Tillicum Rd - Calling in to represent a Langford business. It's
            important to build up, not out.


            Albert Internicola, 670 Marlisa PI - It's people who don't live in the neighbourhood who
            support this. Neighbourhood can't support 113 more vehicles. Do not support.


            Ron Bain, 719 Massie Dr - Do not support, roads are already at maximum capacity.


     Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.


            Tom Miller, 661 Marlisa PI - Do not support, the proposed development is too tall.
            Other people calling in don't understand that the neighbourhood is already dense.


            Albert Internicola, 670 Marlisa PI - Building will shadow neighbourhood, would support
            a smaller building.



            Jacqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Dr - A number of issues with this development
            that were brought up earlier have not been addressed. If approved, the parking
            designation should be Neighbourhood and not City Centre.


     Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the
     Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1856 closed at 6:02 p.m.

candidates.motion_text:
THAT Council:

                     1. Proceed with consideration of Bylaw No. 2019 to amend the zoning
                        designation of the properties located at 982-988 Bray Avenue from
                        One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) to City Centre 1 (CC1) subject
                        to the following terms and conditions:

                         a. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density,
                            the following contributions per dwelling unit, prior to the
                            issuance of a building permit:

                              i.   $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and

                              ii. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

              Subject to reductions in accordance with the Affordable Housing and Amenity
              Contribution Policy and the Attainable Housing Policy depending on use and
              height.

                         b. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section
                            219 covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees
                            to the following:

                              i.   That the following will be provided and implemented to
                                   Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director
                                   of Engineering prior to the issuance of a building permit:

                                   1. Full frontage improvements;







    2. A mitigation plan;

    3. A storm water management plan; and

    4. A construction parking management plan.

ii. That the properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a
    Development Permit for Form and Character;

iii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of
     a building permit for the proposed development that
     ensures residential parking is allocated to each unit and
     visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided
     in exchange for compensation separate from that of a
     residential unit;

iv, That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete
    that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global
    Warming Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline
    (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a
    Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type Ill
    Environmental Product Declaration that is 3rd party verified
    specifying the total Global Warming Potential value and
    confirming that the proposed development meets the
    requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-
    PLAN;

v. That the developer submit the Fire Underwriters Survey
   (FUS) calculations prior to the issuance of a development
   permit to develop the property, and acknowledges that
   these calculations may determiner different setbacks than
   what is prescribed in the zone or from what has been grated
   through variances;

vi. That, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the
    developer enters into a Housing Agreement with the City
    that requires a minimum 10% of units constructed be
    rented at a rate no higher than 30% of the median renter
    income as calculated by the Canadian Mortgage and
    Housing Corporation for Langford for a term not less than
    10 years or that a minimum of 5% of the units constructed
    be directed to and sold in accordance with the terms of the
    Attainable Home Ownership Program Policy (POL-0166-
    PLAN). The developer shall identify the Attainable Units on
    the plans submitted for the required Development Permit
    application.

vii. That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed
     building until a strata plan for the building has been
     registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer.







                    c. Authorize the Director of Planning and Subdivision to issue the
                       following variance in the Form and Character Development
                       Permit for 982-988 Bray Avenue:

                         i.   That Section 6.57.07(1)(b) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be
                              varied to reduce the interior lot line setback of a building or
                              structure from the required 3 m to 2 m.

                    d. Prior to public hearing, the applicant provide the following
                       changes:

                         i. More prominent street presence for ground floor units

                         ii. Design considerations for accessibility and universal design
                             including washer and dryer machines.

                    e. That the proposed car share program and electric heat pumps
                       be provided as a condition of rezoning to the satisfaction of the
                       Director of Engineering and Chief Building Inspector.

                    f.   That the foyer panel is designed to accommodate visual
                         challenges, to the satisfactioh of the Chief Building Inspector.

5.   PUBLIC HEARINGS

     5.1   BYLAW NO. 2126

           "Omnibus No. 61 - Part 3: Unlicensed Vehicles and Institutional Fencing), Bylaw No.
           2126, 2023".

           The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2126 at 7:46 p.m.

           Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that staff are bringing forward Bylaw No.
           2126 which proposes the following amendments to Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
           • Amend the wording within Zoning Bylaw 300 by adding ''unlicensed vehicle" to the list
           of definitions; and
           • Exclude institutional developments from the maximum fence height requirements of
           Zoning Bylaw 300.
           These are proposed to reflect a change in ICBC licensing practices and to give
           institutional uses more flexibility in their specific fencing needs.
           The proposed amendments would be consistent with the City's Official Community Plan.
           Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
           Government Act.

           Mayor Goodmanson called a first time for presentations.

           None presented.

           Mayor Goodmanson called a second time for presentations.

           None presented.

           Mayor Goodmanson called a third time for presenters.

4.          PUBLIC HEARINGS

            4.1    BYLAW NOS. 1989 and 1990

                   The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 1989 and 1990 at 5:35 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Niall Paltiel of Ascend Planning Ltd.
      has applied on behalf of 1103097 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 1300 Valemount Court
      from Attached Housing (RM2A) Zone to the Business Park 2A (BP2A) Zone, and 1289,
      1277; 1265; 1253 Valemount Court from Rural Residential (RR5) to Business Park 2A
      (BP2A) to amend the Official Community Plan designation of the subject properties from
      Hillside or Shoreline to Business or Light Industrial to allow for business type uses to be
      developed on the property.

      1. In support of this application; the applicant has agreed to provide a section 219
      covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title; the following prior to Bylaw
      Adoption:

      a. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades; connections
      and installation of services and utilities required to support the proposed development;
      to the standards of Bylaw No. 1000 and to the satisfaction of the Director of
      Engineering;

      b. That a formal storm water management plan is submitted and implemented prior to
      issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, whichever is first; and
      implemented; as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

      c. That a construction parking and traffic management plan, prepared to the
      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, be provided prior to the issuance of a
      building permit.

      This proposal is consistent with the proposed Official Community Plan "Business or Light
      Industrial" designation

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.


      Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

      N. Paltiel; on behalf of the applicant - presented a Power Point summary of the
      proposed development.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations.

      L. Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Ter - Concerned that the area is heavily forested. Lack of
      amenities means there will be no money coming into the city. Concerned about
      industrial business in residential setting. Will there be property taxation? Ask Council to
      amend the proposal to address concerns.

      Mayor Young declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw Nos. 1989 and 1990 closed at 5:44
      p.m.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 1999


      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1999 at 5:44 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ben Gulbrandsen has applied on
behalf of Jill Moores, Barry Moores, Janis Bayley, Lamar Grube, Patricia Van Buskirk,
Peter Van Buskirk, and Peter Lasell to amend the zoning of 2762, 2768, and 2774
Winster Road from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone to the CCl (City
Centre) Zone.

This is being proposed to allow for the development of a six-storey apartment building.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
bonus for increased density:

a. $750 per unit to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $2,850 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

2. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219
covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

a. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a construction
parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:

b. That the developer registers a strata plan, prior to the issuance of an occupancy
permit, that creates individual strata titles for each residential unit;

c. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
proposed residential building that ensures parking is allocated to each unit and visitors
as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for compensation
separate from that of a residential unit;

d. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
parking space; and

i. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
ii. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
iii. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant from
installing the EV charging equipment.

Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue a variance to
reduce the northern interior side lot line setback from the required 3m to 1.5m for a
stairwell within the Form and Character Development Permit.
This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

      the following:

Permit;

ensure parking is allocated to each unit;
3. That a strata plan is registered for the building prior to issuance of an occupancy
permit;
4.   That 100% of residential parking stalls are capable of providing Level 2 charging for
electric vehicles;
5. That full frontage improvements, a storm water management plan; and a
construction parking management plan be provided and implemented to Bylaw 1000
standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a
building permit.

Plan.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

support the application for the development. Due to a decrease in available sunlight,
displace local habitats, parking concerns, increased traffic issues and safety to the area.
Would like changes to the development size and location.

ideal.

courtyard.

Matthew Baldwin; Director of Planning, responded - that the final design has not been
presented as of yet. Also, that the number of trees to be removed has not been
determined as well.

M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd - Echoes concerns about the removal of trees and the
effects to environment. Would like the developers to save as many trees as possible.

D. Serrao. 792 Revilo PI - Would like the zoning to remain the same. Concerned about
the size of the building, it will remove access to the sunlight. Concerned about the safety
of children on the street due to an increase of traffic. Concerned about the density of
the building. What is the loading zone availability? Would prefer townhomes be built
instead.

C. Harder. 844 Goldstream Ave - Echoes the concerns of the other callers. Would like the
zoning to stay the same. Would like protection of the trees.

K. Cheema. #107-792 Revilo PI - Believes the development should be townhouses.
Would like a lower density building made.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Sherri Davies and Dawn Exiey have
applied to amend the zoning of 661 Hoylake Avenue from the R2 (One- and Two-Family
Residential) Zone to the RTl (Residential Townhouse 1) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately six
townhomes.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
bonus for increased density:

a) $3,660 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
b) $610 per unit to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

1. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219
covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

a) That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards, inclusive of the
construction of a sidewalk, streetlights, scallop parking, and boulevard planting on
Hoylake Avenue, and formalization of the road edge parking on Belair Road, are
provided to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to the issuance of a
building permit;

b) That a Stormwater Management Plan be provided, and all required measures
recommended be implemented by the owner to the satisfaction of the Director of
Engineering, prior to the issuance of a building permit;

c) That a Construction Parking Management Plan be provided to the satisfaction of the
Director of Engineering prior to any alteration of the land.

Council has also, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue the following
setback variances within a form and character development permit:

1. That Section 6.28.07(l)(c) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the exterior
side lot line setback from the required 3.5 m to 0.88 m; and
2. That Section 6.28.07(d) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the rear lot line
setback from the required 5.5 m to 1.2 m, subject to the following condition:

a.   That the interior side lot line have a minimum setback requirement of 5.5 m

designation.

Government Act.

candidates.motion_text:
THAT Committee of the Whole receive this report for information;
               AND
               THAT the Committee recommend that:
               1. Council directs staff to prepare a Standing Internal Borrowing Governance Bylaw for
               Council's consideration, establishing the following minimum requirements for all future
               interfund borrowing under Community Charter:
                       a. The term of any internal loan.
                       b. A formal Internal Loan Agreement.
                       c. The Interest calculated using a publicly defined methodology.
                       d. The specific Internal Loan Agreement and its repayment schedule to be
                       attached as a schedule or appendix to the annual Five-Year Financial Plan Bylaw.
               2. Council directs staff to prepare a Remediation Plan for all internal debt balances
               outstanding as of December 31, 2025, and present this Plan to Council in advance of the
               2027 Financial plan. The Remediation Plan shall include at a minimum:








      Calculate the total accrued foregone interest on all existing internal debt.
      Establish a repayment schedule for all principal and accrued interest, with a specified
      repayment period.
      Identify the proposed funding source for the required interest and principal repayments;
      AND
      3. Council directs staff to amend all relevant policies, to align fully with the requirements
      of the new Internal Borrowing Governance Bylaw once adopted.

records.stored_item_title: Public Hearing Policy

candidates.motion_text:
THAT Council:

             1.   Direct staff to prepare bylaw and/or policy amendments to implement the following:

                     a) That Council makes it their practice to employ Sec. 464(2) of the Local
                     Government Act, unless there are extenuating circumstances that would make it
                     undesirable to do so;
                     b) That the notification procedure for applications where a Public Hearing is
                     not being held (whether prohibited or waived) include: the placement of
                     signage on the subject property at the beginning of the process through the
                     conclusion of the application;
                     c) That the notification procedure for applications where a Public Hearing is
                     not being held (whether prohibited or waived) include, as required,
                     advertisement in a local newspaper prior to 1st reading;
                     d) That the notification procedure for applications where a Public Hearing is
                     not being held (whether prohibited or waived) include written notice to owners
                     and occupiers of land within 100m of the subject property prior to consideration
                     of the application by Committee and again prior to 1st reading;







               e) That the Council Procedure Bylaw be amended to exclude any land use
               bylaw that is being considered for adoption from items that may be discussed
               during the Public Participation portion of Council's meeting; AND
               f) That telecommunications applications be referred to Committee for public
               input, with a recommendation to be approved by Council and forwarded to
               Industry Canada and that the term "Public Hearing" be dropped from this
               process.

3.      PUBUC HEARINGS


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1760
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 522, (804 Latoria Rd and 950
             Worrall Dr), Bylaw No. 1760, 2019".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1760 at 5:30 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Adam Weir, of Langdon Weir Construction Ltd. has
applied on behalf of Ridley Bros. Development Ltd. to amend the zoning of the property at 804 Latoria Road
and 950 Worrall Drive from the RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zone to the RS4, Residential Small Lot 4, Zone and
to add to that zone the following uses for this property only:

                                                                                                   November 25^^ 2019
                                                                                                             Page 2 of 9


            o   Schools
            o   Group Day Cares
            o   Townhouses, not to exceed a total of 80 units;
            o   Small lot single family dwellings, not to exceed a total of 30 units;

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


It was Council's resolution that the applicant provide both a technical stormwater management assessment
and a traffic impact assessment with respect to subject property prior to this Public Hearing and to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering. These have been provided.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a bonus to the City for
increased density in accordance with Council Policy:

          $6000 per one family dwelling towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          $3960 per small lot, one family dwelling towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          $3660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          $1000 per one family dwelling towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
          $660 per small lot, one family dwelling towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
          $610 per townhouse unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

Prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will provide a Section 219 Covenant registered in priority over all
other charges on title that ensures that:

    •   A stormwater management plan is provided and implemented to the satisfaction of the Director of
        Engineering prior to development;
    •   A frontage drawing for Latoria Road is provided to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering,
        and that any road dedication and all required frontage improvements in the Latoria Road corridor
        are provided prior to development and in accordance with the Latoria Road Master Plan and Bylaw
        1000;
    •   That temporary emergency access is provided for with each phase of subdivision, and that water
        flow necessary to comply with Fire Underwriters Survey requirements are provided with each
        proposed phase of development;
    •   That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or other
        servicing requirements are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the
        Director of Engineering and that costs incurred will be the sole responsibility of the applicant;
    •   That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements at their sole cost in accordance with
        Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering for all internal roads;
    •   That the applicant will implement the recommendations of the Traffic Impact Assessment, to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
    •   That the applicant will provide a construction parking management plan to the satisfaction of the
        Director of Engineering prior to issuance of any building permit;

A separate Section 219 covenant is to be registered prior to any subdivision or alteration of the land, and
within this covenant the applicant will agree to provide a Development Concept Plan that secures the layout
of the development, and in particular identifies the following:

                                                                                                          November 25^ 2019
                                                                                                                    Page 3 of 9




    •   The amount and location of trail connections, dedicated open spaces and park spaces;
    •   The amount and location of streamside protection and enhancement areas in accordance with the
        Province's Riparian Areas Regulation and prepared by a Registered Professional Biologist;
    •   The amount and location of covenanted non-disturbance open space outside of the Stream
        Protection and Enhancement Area (SPEA);
    •   The location of the community and recreational amenities; and
    •   The location of the school site; as well as
    •   An estimate of the costs associated with constructing trails and installing park and trail
        infrastructure;

The applicant further agrees, by way of covenant, that there shall be no disturbance or structures within
any of the areas that are designated as non-disturbance areas and that a split-rail fence or stone wall will
be used to delineate these areas from development areas. In the event that any areas designated as non-
disturbance areas, outside of the SPEA, are inadvertently impacted during development the applicant has
agreed to remediate and replant these areas to a natural state in accordance with a planting plan prepared
by a registered professional biologist. SPEA areas will be protected and monitored on site by the project
biologist during construction and site preparation.

With respect to the Riparian areas on with the subject property, the applicant's proposal for dedicated open
space and covenanted open space encompasses all of the SPEA area required by the Province's Riparian
Areas regulation. The actual setback of buildings to the stream will be determined at a later date in the
Development Permit process.

The applicant will also, by way of a covenant, agree to include 10m2 of storage space, exclusive of closet
space, in any single family dwelling on a lot that is less than 400m2.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline designation, and in
particular meets Policy 3.11.1 with respect to the retention of public and/or private open space in Hillside
or Shoreline Areas.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.
